blue-catfish: Anglers are enjoying catching a mix of blue catfish and striped bass in the dam pool close to the turbine wash.
bluefish: This drop in water temperature will drive the spot, bluefish, and red drum south to warmer waters.
Now that the bluefish are gone, gulls resting on the water can offer evidence that some kind of surface action occurred recently.
largemouth-bass: Largemouth bass will be moving more freely throughout the water column and aggressively feeding to build up their body stores for the upcoming winter months.
northern-snakehead: Chesapeake Channa (snakeheads) are starting to feel the chill and sun-soaked shallow water areas during the afternoon are a good place to fish for them.
smallmouth-bass: The upper Potomac waters are running clear and cool this week and offering good fishing for smallmouth bass and walleye.
This will start an exodus of crayfish, which is a smallmouth bass’s favorite food.
striped-bass: The 2026 striped bass young of the year survey results were released this week and although a little better than last year, our striped bass recruitment situation is still a problem.
This will set the stage for striped bass to gather at the mouths of the major tidal rivers and steep channel edges to feed on the baitfish being swept along by stiff currents.
Depth finders will pave the way to spotting suspended striped bass.
walleye: Freshwater Fishing Ryan Chaney holds up a huge walleye he caught recently in the upper Potomac.
The upper Potomac waters are running clear and cool this week and offering good fishing for smallmouth bass and walleye.
white-perch: Anglers in the region’s tidal rivers are finding that white perch are beginning to move to deeper waters.
As water temperature drops this week, white perch may start to head for deeper and warmer waters.
Kent Narrows is worth mentioning as a good place to target white perch this week.
